body:
Founder real-time: "ok iterate on core product work focusing on unblkoccked revenue."

Investigated S135-03 (EDIS WooCommerce sticker listing) first as the most obvious "unblocked
revenue" candidate -- turned out to be genuinely blocked (no sudo password for www-data, no
WooCommerce REST API credentials anywhere, vault locked, no documented unlock). Flagged (Apple
#13349), pivoted to TIPJAR instead.

Found TIPJAR itself was much further along than BACKLOG's own golden-doc entries claimed --
Steps 1 and 2 (SP-SHIFT core loop, player-indexed simulation) were already real and committed
(2026-08-04), contradicting the "zero TIPJAR-specific code exists" note that's now stale. Real
next roadmap step: Step 3, split-screen. Implemented the 2P slice (3P/4P is real, scoped
follow-up, not done here):

- local_game.h: new local_set_player_input(player_id, ...) -- local_update previously hardcoded
  player 0 only; every other active slot fell through to bot_think or sat with stale input.
  Backward compatible, zero change to local_update's existing signature/behavior for player 0.
- main.c: TIPJAR now activates a real players[1] (local_init_match(2,...) + is_bot=0 override),
  reads a second keyboard scheme (arrows + RCtrl/RShift/Slash/Apostrophe, no conflicts with P1's
  WASD/Space/J/K/LShift), feeds both TipjarPlayerInput rows, and renders two real glViewport
  panels (left/right halves of the fixed 1280x720 window) each with its own camera centered on
  its owning player -- matches the wiki's own G0.2 "couch-style visibility" goal.

Verified for real, not just compiled: Xvfb + python-xlib (XTest) launch, keypress simulation,
screenshot capture. Confirmed both panels render correctly with independent HUD/camera, confirmed
both players respond to their own real input, confirmed shift timer counts down correctly in real
time (debug-instrumented, temporarily, then removed) across 25+ real seconds of live movement --
an early anomalous "SHIFT OVER" observation during ad hoc testing did not reproduce under
controlled, repeated, debug-logged conditions and is most likely a one-off test-environment
artifact from this session's already very heavy concurrent system load, not a real defect;
flagged honestly rather than either hidden or over-fixed blind.

Physics smoke test (tests/test_physics.c) passes. Real follow-up work, not done here: 3P/4P
split, gamepad support for player 2 (engine only has one ControllerState today).
title: TIPJAR Step 3: real 2-player local split-screen
